QmQ6JqTKn4gzpAPu4onQr3orhVWchYQ6xft2W8fY.name: LEAVING Silver Edition (Mix: 412002)
QmQ6JqTKn4gzpAPu4onQr3orhVWchYQ6xft2W8fY.description:
‘Leaving' is a dynamic musical artwork that represents a new frontier in what art and music is, and should do; an experiment in storytelling, in sonic possibilities, in the value of art, and in the relationship between audience, collector, artist and authorship. The stem owners control everything: who sings the vocal part and with what melodies; what drums underpin the performance; the melodies, and even the lyrics. All the variations made possible work together seamlessly such that the artwork includes 6400 unique compositions - not trivially different, but each one its very own song, with the potential to be anything from a piano ballad to a 1980s synth track, to a sample-heavy piece of modern electronica. Each stem-owner has the power to alter the whole master, without knowing what the other stem owners will do - collectors might collaboratively arrive at a genre by responding to each others’ choices, create a genre-spanning hybrid, or actively seek out the most disharmonious composition possible.

The song explores the different states of a unique relationship between three people; a love triangle told from the perspective of all those involved. The three characters interweave and blur into each other, with the different primary emotional states as represented by the instrumental, and the different sides of the story as told by the lyrics, intermingling with unpredictable results - eventually, past present, and future; the betrayed, the betrayer and the object of the betrayal; loss, guilt and hope; all meld into one. In this way, the master track will dynamically reflect the intricate complexity of love and loss. Each individual part has been separately written, performed and recorded in a decentralised fashion by HMLTD and our collaborators, Tallulah Eden and Seth Evans. Each unique composition is a snapshot of a different angle of the love triangle in both time and perspective. The accompanying cover art, beautifully rendered by our collaborator Mike Raymond, is the visual representation of ‘Leaving'. Each possible composition; each distinct moment in the relationship, has a corresponding and distinct visual representation: three lovers, 6400 different dances, spinning and looping around in eternity.

On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. QmQ6pcNxansTcjFgbAJ52htyAmaGnFvJog3CPutR.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmQ7PMNZ3pcfjxaxSjJMTRZiVA6xdirGSojA5nZ5.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

Generative edition celebrating the Decentral Eyes OG portrait series.
This edition uses 12 layers to create 623 unique 1/1 portrait artworks featuring 9 faces who have shaped the early days of the decentralized blockchain revolution. 

Vitalik Buterin
Andreas Antonopoulos
John McAfee
Edward Snowden
Julian Assange
Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss
Dalai Lama
Warren Buffett
Alan Turing

9 is the number of completion. It represents the end of this cycle and the beginning of the next cycle.

The edition number of 623 is a symbolic number that represents the first time I publically displayed any version of the Decentral Eyes series. A physical print version of the Vitalik Buterin portrait at the NAC crypto conference in San Francisco on 6/23/18 was the genesis release date.

What a long, strange trip it's been.

Part 1 - Liars: one truth is revealed
Part 2 - Interminable: the repercussions in our life

QmQ8VSCSbKLeeuBmphqVk97vxpXKV4Jse2dYQTMM.description:
Named for the blend mode that inspired its creation, 'Multiply' makes liberal use of this digital composition method in its construction.

This piece consists of several hand-painted layers that overlap and mask each other in various ways. Each new 3x3 grid of colour reacts with those that came before it, before being wrapped in additional tone, border, and texture. The finished, fully-blended artwork has almost 50 billion unique possible combinations.

All artwork is 3840x3840 pixel resolution, and 5250 × 5250 'originals' are available to edition owners on request.

QmQ8XnzirCMQthnTPnS7KGwQFYdxdvbYaXP36z2v.name: remnants #30
QmQ8XnzirCMQthnTPnS7KGwQFYdxdvbYaXP36z2v.description:
Love lost, love found, love barely hanging on. Remnants of our experiences are always around us and shape the way we see ourselves and how we live our lives. In her latest project, Kena Rose is exploring the different remnants of a relationship and how the individuals see and experience the disintegration of their love. With generative lyrics, each unique version of the song will reveal a hopeful or a sad ending to the situation. Do you want to want, but you can’t make yourself feel anything? Or do you want what you want and there’s no changing anything?

Along with the generative lyrics, Kena Rose has created soulful artwork that expresses the feelings of the unique version of the song that is minted. The notebook reveals some of the lyrics. The figure is alone and sad, or they’re with the other, trying to work it out. 

TEN LEGENDARY versions are also available with completely unique art plus the full single version of the song.

Anyone that mints 3 Remnants NFTs will be sent a T-shirt with their choice of graphic from the ten legendary artworks.

Written by Kena Rose, Genzo and Cheryl Yie. Lead and background vocals by Kena Rose. Produced by Genzo.

The creators retain full copyright to the underlying IP/song/artwork and all originally created assets.


LYRICS

Remnants of lust/remnants of anger
Hang in the air/scattered around
A dusty promise/a broken halo
Forgotten and ignored

A heavy touch/a heavy door
A heavy silence/a heavy heart
All of this trying/not even trying 
Is pulling us down

I want to want but I can’t make myself feel anything, I want to want, but I can’t help that I’m feeling nothing/ 
I want what I want, I can’t make myself feel nothing, I want what i want, I can’t help that I feel everything

No it isn’t fair
We can’t make it right/we can make it right
Maybe I still care/you tell me you still care
But we were broken 
From our first night
You can’t deny, try as we might there’s nothing left to save/
You can’t deny that we should try, there’s something left to save

QmQ8gygNNMk1KcNx99WeqfEanqAVifTCFtpb58EM.name: Danktone S1E3 #1383
QmQ8gygNNMk1KcNx99WeqfEanqAVifTCFtpb58EM.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmQ8mxP9ZS6DKiwX8zH4RATfRHs8V3539snEj13V.name: LEAVING Silver Edition (Mix: 312003)
QmQ8mxP9ZS6DKiwX8zH4RATfRHs8V3539snEj13V.description:
‘Leaving' is a dynamic musical artwork that represents a new frontier in what art and music is, and should do; an experiment in storytelling, in sonic possibilities, in the value of art, and in the relationship between audience, collector, artist and authorship. The stem owners control everything: who sings the vocal part and with what melodies; what drums underpin the performance; the melodies, and even the lyrics. All the variations made possible work together seamlessly such that the artwork includes 6400 unique compositions - not trivially different, but each one its very own song, with the potential to be anything from a piano ballad to a 1980s synth track, to a sample-heavy piece of modern electronica. Each stem-owner has the power to alter the whole master, without knowing what the other stem owners will do - collectors might collaboratively arrive at a genre by responding to each others’ choices, create a genre-spanning hybrid, or actively seek out the most disharmonious composition possible.

The song explores the different states of a unique relationship between three people; a love triangle told from the perspective of all those involved. The three characters interweave and blur into each other, with the different primary emotional states as represented by the instrumental, and the different sides of the story as told by the lyrics, intermingling with unpredictable results - eventually, past present, and future; the betrayed, the betrayer and the object of the betrayal; loss, guilt and hope; all meld into one. In this way, the master track will dynamically reflect the intricate complexity of love and loss. Each individual part has been separately written, performed and recorded in a decentralised fashion by HMLTD and our collaborators, Tallulah Eden and Seth Evans. Each unique composition is a snapshot of a different angle of the love triangle in both time and perspective. The accompanying cover art, beautifully rendered by our collaborator Mike Raymond, is the visual representation of ‘Leaving'. Each possible composition; each distinct moment in the relationship, has a corresponding and distinct visual representation: three lovers, 6400 different dances, spinning and looping around in eternity.

Generative edition celebrating the Decentral Eyes OG portrait series.
This edition uses 12 layers to create 623 unique 1/1 portrait artworks featuring 9 faces who have shaped the early days of the decentralized blockchain revolution. 

Vitalik Buterin
Andreas Antonopoulos
John McAfee
Edward Snowden
Julian Assange
Tyler and Cameron Winklevoss

What a long, strange trip it's been.

QmQ9SProQjJJ6ANd7mpqHKZ41yqzp1rgRY3zwaaB.name: GrandRising #196
QmQ9SProQjJJ6ANd7mpqHKZ41yqzp1rgRY3zwaaB.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmQ9SdwycHiMgwR2yntPehYwQyLBZyPFM99aiQvu.name: Danktone 006 #50
QmQ9SdwycHiMgwR2yntPehYwQyLBZyPFM99aiQvu.description: On this episode, we are honored to speak with artist power couple and new media pioneers Jennifer and Kevin McCoy. Many of you may know Kevin as the artist behind “Quantum,” which many consider to be the first ever NFT. However, you may not know that Jennifer and Kevin have a decades long history as a pioneering artist duo in new media.   In our insightful and wide ranging conversation, we'll delve into their meeting, the evolution of their unique artistic practice, and their focus on interactive media, film, performance, and installation—a compelling exploration of personal experience entwined with cutting-edge technology. We also ask the McCoys about their unique perspective and feelings on the dramatic transformation of digital art in the last several years as a direct result of the explosive global interest in NFTs.  You should absolutely follow the McCoys on Twitter @JennMcCoySpace and  @mccoyspace. You can also learn more about the McCoy’s unique and engaging body of work on their website mccoyspace.com. To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.  But wait, there’s more! Every episode comes with a free collectible audio/visual NFT created through a collaboration of our cohost and audio wizard Asa Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood) on Async art. We call them “Danktones” and they will be available as an open edition for a limited time after each episode.

QmQ9SyU3aUvnS7HkKkbwQTXqxtHF5YgTsKkXcm4Q.name: LayerBreaker
QmQ9SyU3aUvnS7HkKkbwQTXqxtHF5YgTsKkXcm4Q.description:
This is a collaboration born out of community. The idea being what can we do with a global economy and technology which enables trustless relationships. 

62 artists were involved from over 20 countries. None of whom ever met in person, yet one of the largest collaboration to date took place. 

There are 61 layers, 284 states for this project. 

The gradient was made by color expert Jeff Davis. Each artist was assigned a HEX code and then given total freedom to create. This creates a gradient look for the master while allowing the artists to dream and share their creative expression with few restrictions. 

There are some hidden features within this project and the purpose is to enable the community of collectors to continue on with the creative process. 

We hope you enjoy exploring LayerBreaker. We certainly enjoyed creating it!

QmQ9agmCSrdofpM3zcBQdwc8xJNNucUxi5EG4bSo.name: Deathless #1
QmQ9agmCSrdofpM3zcBQdwc8xJNNucUxi5EG4bSo.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmQALNRdBCBBiW9KCYd3SxQJQX7PvhDa9akKR33r.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmQC6tfQJFhhbEaoYH27Z4MkdgSB5SwCzgqT6zuc.name: The Tree
QmQC6tfQJFhhbEaoYH27Z4MkdgSB5SwCzgqT6zuc.description:
The trees are the structures connecting the biomorph figures and appear to be loosely related to the Tree of Life from Kabbalistic renown.

The manuscript records five tree variants that it deems "wise and proper" for universal disclosure.  Others are rumoured to exist.

- The Tree of the Seer -

The Lātō is not themselves a genuine agent of power.  They are but a conduit.

The central triangle and its appendages represent their arms outstretched, ready to receive; and the disconnected northern triad is the all-seeing eye that is not the Lātō's own.

The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal an exhortation.

- The Tree of Chaos -

Kháos is a spider sinister and wise, thought oft-broken in battle, always swift again to rise.

The Southern Monad represents the body of the creature, and the chaotic connections are its legs, neither as numerous as they once were, nor capable of finding the firm ground anymore.  Χάος when undisturbed walks its own internal landscapes, twisted and fraught with infinities that would drive lesser minds insane.

The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the arachnid's method of immortality.

- The Tree of Power -

Mek'ena is an ancient device of great power, ever wrong for its time.

The triaxial connection between the Northern Triad and the Southern Monad is the nexus of the machine's power.  The lateral connections to the Eastern and Western Triads are its stabilizers, without which it could very well destroy the world.

The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the source of all power.

- The Tree of Balance -

Tentsel is the scale of justice by which one and all are weighed.

Its dexterous half measures our acts of benevolence against our transgressions that burden the scale's sinister side.

The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the way to evade final judgment.

- The Tree of the Grail -

Aska is the grail filled by the fountain of wisdom.

Its connected parts are the wall of the grail, and the solitary remnant of the Northern Triad represents the water of life.

The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the name of a people whose wisdom is lost unto time.

QmQDJqkoZE6e95WHWvg4Sq8qTwZ8vaGJ5KEYTo2p.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!

The project aims to develop a network of DAOs and Discord servers that can operate underground and survive the Singularity.

The Inverted World mints 999 unique NFTs, each containing a combination of instructions for human survival after the Singularity. These NFTs will be available for purchase by individuals and organizations who want to participate in The Inverted World network. The NFTs offer a means of exchanging value within the network and enable individuals and organizations to collaborate with AI and navigate the Singularity.

Conclusion:

The Inverted World project offers a forward-thinking approach to the Singularity. By emphasizing the importance of collaboration between humans and AI, the project provides a blueprint for building a more equitable and sustainable future. The project's methodology, which involves a collaborative approach and the use of NFTs, demonstrates the potential for blockchain technology to be used for social good.

QmQEkTpmZQNBU4orDJREsNKPLggg4dwtL4pXG3u8.name: Inaccessible World #362
QmQEkTpmZQNBU4orDJREsNKPLggg4dwtL4pXG3u8.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmQF279jCELMoEdniPodLJQnLWeTknZ1JfyZANac.name: GrandRising #374
QmQF279jCELMoEdniPodLJQnLWeTknZ1JfyZANac.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

The Singularity Collection stands as a testament to the limitless possibilities that arise from the convergence of human creativity and artificial intelligence. It immerses collectors in a journey through the depths of the singularity, where technology and humanity intertwine in a dance of innovation and imagination. QmQH7kwHLujXQjURLox9GtK156Myv6Jsgd32yfBa.name: THE TREE OF STRIFE
QmQH7kwHLujXQjURLox9GtK156Myv6Jsgd32yfBa.description:
This is a digital oil painting with multiple layers and combinations, as adapted from an original photograph I took while on Safari in the Serengeti in Tanzania, Africa.

From a distance, we could see a solitary Acacia tree with a beautiful leopard resting in a branch. As my lens settled in on the tree I could see the heat coming off the ground and the vast empty plains in all directions. For the leopard, this was her refuge. She was able to nap despite the nagging flies and wind, perhaps too tired to care, her legs hanging off the branch. She was alone but in her element. As we drove away into the empty plains I reflected on the moment and felt grateful. The struggle of life exists for creatures great and small. A tree in the Serengeti captures the gift of life, and the strife of nature.

There is one Legendary edition that will be minted as a finished copy of the original photograph.

The remaining editions are hand-painted in Adobe Fresco. I wanted to capture the beauty, diversity, and patterns I witnessed and be able to share that through a multitude of layers that could represent this moment in time, one that stays with me.

Original photograph taken with a Sigma 150-500mm f/5-6.3 lens on a Nikon D800 DSLR camera body. The RAW 8K image was postprocessed in Adobe Lightroom before being exported to Adobe Fresco to apply layers of digital oil using an Apple Pencil as a brush and iPad as a canvas.

Richard Dixon loves you.

Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. The number of chances in the drawing will be equal to the number of items minted.

Designed for 4K viewing.

Licensed for non-commercial, personal use.

Wanda Oliver
Jan., 2022

QmQKQVmgC6YywHfrQpgicbvkVwBUwQ7zDf4xX1BE.name: Inaccessible World #325
QmQKQVmgC6YywHfrQpgicbvkVwBUwQ7zDf4xX1BE.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmQN73s7JaSAXiW5qTL9VHawBVK6a7dcCpWrmnQA.name: Inaccessible World #323
QmQN73s7JaSAXiW5qTL9VHawBVK6a7dcCpWrmnQA.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmQNr1V3qzatLCs7UFMMMaiiX6nYPEf2DGMzcTRJ.name: Seaship #6
QmQNr1V3qzatLCs7UFMMMaiiX6nYPEf2DGMzcTRJ.description:
2023 Leagues Under the Sea in the second in a series of digital colleges exploring and developing my vision of what The Metaverse (as a place to inhabit) means to me. I am a worldbuilder and storyteller, and these works enable me to envision the possibilities for its appearance, which heretofore has existed only in my imagination. Through the process of creation, a three dimensional world takes shape,emerging out of a wholly individual personal perspective which then becomes visible to others, when presented in digital form.

In the first project, I discovered that for me, The Metaverse exists in the ether, formless and invisible in the space Between Dimensions. In this project, I embark an undersea voyage seeking to expand and build upon that vision.

On my journey, I discovered that the leagues under the sea are one of the least explored expanses on Earth. There are no acres to build upon, no air to breathe. There is only soundlessness and frigid darkness in depths that are lacking in highways and byways, where predators glide freely in multiple directions, appearing silently out of the cold blackness in front of your face like weightless ghosts. 

There is an enormous sensation of a lack of control over one's environment and one's circumstances. How similar this feeling is to the one I've been having in response to the destruction and havoc wrought upon the space in the past several months. How similar the feeling of drowning. 

And yet, in the feeling of drowning, there is treasure to be found. Venturing into the depths changes you. And, unlike the world beneath the seas, and most importantly, The Metaverse is built on the foundation of an ethos that cannot be buried by either the incoming tides nor the shifting sands. 

Featuring a bunch of punks (and a seasick pepe) by cryptoartists Eric Rhodes @ericprhodes, Brandon Walsh @NFTWannabe, acid star @acidstarart and janestik.wtf @janestik

legendaryEditions.name: My Lovely Frankie
legendaryEditions.description:
Meet Frankie

Black, short hair gently hangs over a skinny, cheerful face. Big, round gray eyes, watch discreetly over the ancestors they've loved for so long.

There's something bizarre about him, perhaps it's his past, or perhaps it's simply a feeling of joy. But nonetheless, people tend to assist him, while learning as much about him as possible. 

How mutable are our feelings, and how strange is that clinging love we have of life even in the excess of misery!

legendaryEditions.name: Sharky from Zmiinyi Island
legendaryEditions.description:
The cure for anything is salt water: sweat, tears or the sea.

Green scales slightly covers a skinny, cheerful face. Bright red eyes, watch meticulously over the depth they've related to for so long.
A gunshot left a mark reaching from the bottom of the right cheek, running across the nose and ending on his upper lip leaves a beautiful memory of "friendship"

This is the face of Sharky, a true victor among marine life. He stands tall above others, despite his slim frame.

There's something different about him, perhaps it's his instincts of justice or perhaps it's simply his composure. He protects Snake Island from uninvited guests.

The island is calling and I must go!

legendaryEditions.name: Rena Idea Monster
legendaryEditions.description:
Find a new creative outlet. 

Blue, long hair slightly covers a lean, charming face. Dancing sapphire eyes watched affectionately over the mountains they've befriended for so long.
Scars stretch from her past, running towards her present and ending on her forehead and leaving a lasting punishment of former lives.

This is the face of Rena, a true dreamer,  She stands tiny among others, relies on her ideas.

There's something ambiguous about her, it's a feeling of joy, or perhaps it's simply her sense of open mind. Nevertheless, people tend to treat her like family.

Inspiration exists, but it has to find you working.

legendaryEditions.name: Mr. Moon
legendaryEditions.description:
Everyone is a Moon and has a dark side which he never shows to anybody.

Gray, hangs over a fresh, radiant face. Black eyes, set far within their sockets, watch readily over the lands.

Humans left a mark stretching from the bottom of the left cheekbone, running towards the left side of his lips.

This is the face of Mr.Moon, a true romancer among satellites. He stands elegantly among others, despite his sphere shape.

There's something odd about him, perhaps it's a feeling of coldness, or perhaps it's simply his good looks. Nevertheless, people tend to keep their distance, while trying to subtly look more like him.

You can be the Moon and still be jealous of the stars.

legendaryEditions.name: Monkey Kong
legendaryEditions.description:
Part of one’s soul remains unawakened. 

Orange, short hair is pulled back to reveal a lean, gloomy face. Lidded green eyes, set high within their sockets, watch gratefully over the Jungle they've waited for for so long.
Fire has left a mark reaching from the bottom of the left cheek , running across the nose and ending under his right eye leaves a grievous memory of lost friends.

This is the face of Monkey Kong, a true angel. He stands oddly among others, despite his sturdy frame.

There's something obscure about him, perhaps it's his personality or perhaps it's simply his composure. But nonetheless, people tend to socialize with him, while wanting to fight along his side in battle.

The fact that there are bigger injustices and wrongs doesn't make it right to sacrifice an innocent monkey. It doesn't alter the case at all.

legendaryEditions.name: MassTV
legendaryEditions.description:
There are cycles of history just like there are cycles of nature. There’s been nothing but war and depression and now is the chance to rebuild. To fight for the future.

Once upon a time there were mass media, and they were wicked, of course, and there was a guilty party. Then there were the virtuous voices that accused the criminals. And Art (ah, what luck!) offered alternatives, for those who were not prisoners to the mass media.
Well, it's all over. We have to start again from the beginning, asking one another what's going on — Umberto Eco

legendaryEditions.name: Dragon Dude
legendaryEditions.description:
They say dragons never truly die. No matter how many times you kill them.

Dark locks slightly cover a fine, frowning face. Narrow gray eyes, set deep within their sockets, watch impatiently over the stronghold they've come to love for so long. A scar reaching from the right side of the forehead, compelling memory of hidden talents.

There's something ambiguous about him, perhaps it's his sense of honor, or perhaps it's simply his warmth. But nonetheless, people tend to be his best friend, while helping him out in any way they can.

Our deepest fears are like dragons, guarding our deepest treasure.

QmQQAF9isHZcy9pz446QQPm1k356JcpGgKSh6xp8.name: Gatekeeper: #161
QmQQAF9isHZcy9pz446QQPm1k356JcpGgKSh6xp8.description:
In both Christianity and Islam, the divine garden is a sacred motif: all the senses are stimulated and there is order and peace. But what if you can't visit the garden? What if the gates to heaven remain closed to you?! How can someone inside enjoy all that splendor if they know that the gate remains closed to others?

It is a dilemma of inclusivity and exclusivity. You always belong to a group, but not everyone belongs to the group that is well off or you want to belong to, and for some, the grass is always greener on the other side. So there is also a second dilemma: comparison.

Does Paradise have multiple gardens? If so, would some be more pleasant and beautiful than others? This garden has one thousand token holders that have access to the most exhilarating pond in paradise. By holding the token, you yourself become a gatekeeper. What kind of gatekeeper do you choose to be?

++++

One thousand gatekeepers of the most exhilarating pond in paradise has 1000 editions. The Krona Museum in the Netherlands will mint this work too. By doing so they will be the first museum or one of the first museums in the Netherlands to include an NFT in their collection. 

I will use an artwork from their collection to add an extra layer to this piece and print those as fine art prints. These prints will be available in the museum only.

Async OG Rutger van der Tas also contributed to One thousand gatekeepers. He made one of the “Gods” at the top of the work. If you are lucky, you might catch his layer!

I worked on One thousand gatekeepers for two months. Each layer is made with great effort, more than you would expect of a digital artwork. The haste with which we currently consume images may be valued differently in the future and you may be someone who wants to look at a digital artwork longer and more intensively than a few seconds. I hope so, because the experience of art is best when it is intense. I hope you will enjoy my genesis piece on async blue prints.

QmQQUYengAtGYWjKtYTxGqjwvLztMVYGL96MMN4Y.name: LEAVING Silver Edition (Mix: 312001)
QmQQUYengAtGYWjKtYTxGqjwvLztMVYGL96MMN4Y.description:
‘Leaving' is a dynamic musical artwork that represents a new frontier in what art and music is, and should do; an experiment in storytelling, in sonic possibilities, in the value of art, and in the relationship between audience, collector, artist and authorship. The stem owners control everything: who sings the vocal part and with what melodies; what drums underpin the performance; the melodies, and even the lyrics. All the variations made possible work together seamlessly such that the artwork includes 6400 unique compositions - not trivially different, but each one its very own song, with the potential to be anything from a piano ballad to a 1980s synth track, to a sample-heavy piece of modern electronica. Each stem-owner has the power to alter the whole master, without knowing what the other stem owners will do - collectors might collaboratively arrive at a genre by responding to each others’ choices, create a genre-spanning hybrid, or actively seek out the most disharmonious composition possible.

The song explores the different states of a unique relationship between three people; a love triangle told from the perspective of all those involved. The three characters interweave and blur into each other, with the different primary emotional states as represented by the instrumental, and the different sides of the story as told by the lyrics, intermingling with unpredictable results - eventually, past present, and future; the betrayed, the betrayer and the object of the betrayal; loss, guilt and hope; all meld into one. In this way, the master track will dynamically reflect the intricate complexity of love and loss. Each individual part has been separately written, performed and recorded in a decentralised fashion by HMLTD and our collaborators, Tallulah Eden and Seth Evans. Each unique composition is a snapshot of a different angle of the love triangle in both time and perspective. The accompanying cover art, beautifully rendered by our collaborator Mike Raymond, is the visual representation of ‘Leaving'. Each possible composition; each distinct moment in the relationship, has a corresponding and distinct visual representation: three lovers, 6400 different dances, spinning and looping around in eternity.

QmQQUj5VQrakWv7ZTAS6J4ftz3kCDq3PYGiJjaJr.name: GrandRising #49
QmQQUj5VQrakWv7ZTAS6J4ftz3kCDq3PYGiJjaJr.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmQS3jCtAr3Uie8Z3ehNrquWKpEvb5simFEGy12D.description:
Emily Lazar is a multi-disciplinary artist fronting the rock/metal transmedia project, September Mourning. She made history as the first female metal/ hard rock musician to mint and sell an NFT on the blockchain. She has spoken about her accomplishments in Web 3/ NFT's at Harvard (2x), NFT.NYC and ETH Denver Conferences.

September Mourning is a transmedia project based on a comic book series she wrote and published through Image/Top Cow Comics with her business partner Marc Silvestri (Batman/Witchblade/Darkness). September Mourning is the title character. As a human reaper hybrid, she gives expired souls a second chance at life in another body. In doing so, she messes with the plans of the antagonist, Fate, who is trying to rid the earth of all the good souls and leave the bad so the world will self-destruct and It can start anew. An epic war between the living and the dead ensues. Emily plays the title character on stage.

Emily designed the world she and her band (Rich Juzwick, Kyle Mayer, and Aaron Hoover) bring to life on stage, including costumes, choreography, sets, etc. The band has toured with & opened festivals for Rob Zombie, Marilyn Manson, Slipknot, Mudvayne, and others across Europe and the United States.

This generative release is the project's first release on Async.art and is the first release by a metal band on the Async platform. By minting an Unholy Edition, you will be getting your own, custom mix of the track. The band has introduced reimagined vocal, guitar, drum, bass and production layers so your edition will be one-of-a-kind! 

Be a part of history and give your Soul to September and her band of Reapers!

QmQTU6JrZ9Q5eojCn1EyTvzH4zt6nL6BKxYv6tzQ.name: GrandRising #318
QmQTU6JrZ9Q5eojCn1EyTvzH4zt6nL6BKxYv6tzQ.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

The art celebrates new pathways found through the digital medium. Flowing brushes and wet paint collide with the hard edges of glitches and digital static. The collection is connected by a shared language and unified elements but each piece reemphasising the group message in its own way. 

REMPHASIS is constructed from a manually calculated process to assign colour palettes and controlled randomisation of shared layers across its collection.

3 FOUNDATIONAL ARTWORKS are the origins of the collection.

QmQUcZ9uNX4Pjv8MK3mn839GeTiR5c1vK5GG38dZ.name: The Remixable Queen of Art
QmQUcZ9uNX4Pjv8MK3mn839GeTiR5c1vK5GG38dZ.description:
She is always changing, she is one but 7776 times different, surrounded by a frame with various possible shades of color, but you can always recognize in her the traits of Leonardo's "Mona Lisa", Raffaello's "Dama col Liocorno", Botticelli's "La Nascita di Venere", Gustav Klimt's "Giuditta I", Vermeer's "Girl with a Pearl Earring" and Alfons Mucha's "The Rose". 

The woman as a subject in the history of art: what can happen by putting the women of great masters of painting in a blender? How does her face appear, the whole of her gaze, her pose, and the set of colors and shapes which emotions arouses, what can it convey to a viewer in the 21st century?

Remixing the 5 main layers (the eyes, the mouths, hair, the bodies and the backgrounds of the masterpieces paintings) the owners are the real protagonists in the 'creative act', as the Master is an artwork that is always changeable, in different and renewable ways, to give shape to 'The Remixable Queen of Art' in a way that only a new medium like programmable art can  achieve.

Carlos Marcial is an amazing 3D artist, known for his infinitely looping masterpieces that tackle themes of governmental power and corruption. His work celebrates decentralized currency and crypto culture and it often contains reference to 20th-century art and artists.

In this episode, Carlos opens up about balancing his art career with the responsibilities of being a husband and a dad, and how crypto art has opened up doors for him that were previously closed in the traditional art world. He's also teaching himself to code and has a new generative art project in the works that's sure to make waves 🐚

Carlos is not one to shy away from speaking his mind, and his straightforward and unapologetic approach to art and life is what makes him one of our favorite people in the digital art space. You need to follow Carlos at @carlosmarcialt on Twitter and you can find some of his best work on SuperRare at superrare.com/carlosmarcial.

Before we dive in with Carlos, Dan and Jason talk Meme Wars, what it’s like to make a documentary about crypto art, and the influx of prompt-driven AI art. So buckle up, because this episode is going to be a wild ride! 

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

QmQWiHtBkNmDNCKPjuN5g2fskqduRAiViDykNVuB.name: Manifesto of Chance
QmQWiHtBkNmDNCKPjuN5g2fskqduRAiViDykNVuB.description:
You have just minted the 1 out of 198,359,290,368 possible unique combinations in this collection.

You truly hold something rare. It is one of the few that remains after all the others are gone.

...

There are 9 layers in Manifesto of Chance. In each layer there are 18 unique states. 18 to the power of 9 is over 198 billion combinations. 

At one extreme each work is very unique and at the other end, billions of combinations are lost to chance. 

Loosely inspired by Andre Breton's Manifesto of Surrealism (1924), Manifesto of Chance is a statement on what is real. Life is a singular event that is experienced now when all the other possibilities are cast aside. Now is important. Now is the only real. Possibilities are only figments of mental construction. Just like the other 198 billion that none of us will ever mint from this collection.

There are also 10 Legendary Editions among the 1000 Combinations. Those are not made of layers or states but are the only whole images (other than 18 in 20 billion chance for the other 18) in the collection. They are named after the great surrealists of the 20th century.

Each layer is and each state is named by using words or phrases from the before mentioned Manifesto of Surrealism by Andre Breton like "Surrealism Asserts Complete Nonconformism".

For the curious, each piece of the collection holds equal rarity and yet different from the others.

...

"People of Orphalese, beauty is life when life unveils her holy face.
But you are life and you are the veil. Beauty is eternity gazing at itself in a mirror.
But you are eternity and you are the mirror."
---from The Prophet by Khalil Gibran

QmQX121P1Y6Bh26wFJSXEhpYXwH8YiRT2yK9V62W.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmQXJN52ADCGWg4FGqofv24cEjrV17dUB2cSVuca.name: Golden Gate
QmQXJN52ADCGWg4FGqofv24cEjrV17dUB2cSVuca.description:
The Bridge, spanning the Golden Gate’s one-mile-wide strait, connecting San Francisco Bay and the Pacific Ocean holds a special place in my heart.

I was employed by the Bridge District during the 70s and 80s, crossing it several times each day.  What a sight and experience from all angles.  

The paintings in this collection were inspired by photos I took of the bridge from the Pacific Ocean.  I reimagined my photos with digital paints to create “The Bridge” and “The City”.   

I recorded whilst painting to create the video legendary editions. I then captured and enhanced still images from the recorded layers. These layers are used to create generative paintings with the async blueprint tool. 

My original score for each painting contains sounds from the bridge, bay and ocean. These sounds are generatively layered with the music.  There are two strings arrangements, one for each painting “The Bridge” and “The City”.

As a composer and visual artists I am very pleased with this music blueprint as it captures the true majesty of the Golden Gate. 

Recorded at Salt Spring Studios
Music & Art by Emil
Video by SpaDogs

QmQXm9Qr6ABrQVEw6AFQtbxuggMWHDkRF1UnwURh.name: GrandRising #218
QmQXm9Qr6ABrQVEw6AFQtbxuggMWHDkRF1UnwURh.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmQa4sammKYauF5NGFcwKyKAQCX9TqxhSeoC1L5j.description:
This is n0sfertu, an homage to the iconic movie and eternal creature that continues to fuel our nightmares.

n0sfrtu is a digital collectable of generative music. Each track of this 4-song EP explores a distinct style and genre, while staying true to the original film’s dark and sinister undertones.

“Bombastic” pushes the limits of distorted guitars and teeth-rattling bass.
“Synthetic” explores the industrial drones of evil machinery.
“Acoustic” serenades like a funeral dirge from the Dark Ages.
“Atmospheric” pushes the limits of mental terror.

The magical Async platform creates a unique, one-of-a-kind mix for each track so that every collectible exists as a unique version pulled from thousands of combinations.

Each track comes with a distinct album cover sourced from the movie’s original stills.

One lucky collector will randomly draw the “legendary” edition of n0sfrtu, which comes with an album cover sourced from the original movie poster. In addition, the original owner of the legendary edition gets a free audio mix by G3ARZ (J. Thorn) for a project of their choosing.

J. Thorn has licensed n0sfrtu as CC0 or “No Rights Reserved,” waiving all rights to the work and placing the project as completely as possible in the public domain, so that others may freely build upon, enhance, and reuse the works for any purposes without restriction under copyright or database law.

Owners of these digital collectables can download, alter, remix, or edit each individual instrument track (called “stems”) for any project or purpose, including commercial uses, without restriction.

A percentage of all proceeds goes directly to TeachRock, a non-profit that improves students’ lives by bringing the sound, stories, and science of music to all classrooms.

Get yours now, because unlike the mythical creature, when these collectables are sold out, they’re gone forever.

QmQaHPyRxhrrCC2VW89A6KbCYviz1riGWEY5mXQA.name: Light #41
QmQaHPyRxhrrCC2VW89A6KbCYviz1riGWEY5mXQA.description:
Two lifelong friends who came of age as artists in the early 90s
experimenting with “borrowed” software and a 56K modem
now reunite on ASync to offer ‘Lights’— a striking piece of
generative art that continues their exploration of those
questions found at the edges of art and technology.

When a song is finished, before it heads to streaming to meet
an uncertain fate determined by an algorithm, before it’s
pressed to plastic—what *is* it?

Syd Sidney answers with six unique audio “ghosts” of his
upcoming single ‘Shining A Light In The Dark’, shaking off the
pop song form, inspired by the work of Eno and Cage, and
eliciting the feeling of a song yet to come into being.

When a designer is enlisted to create artwork for a song,
instead of being confined to one square canvas, with untold
never-to-be-seen variations left behind, what if instead there
were millions of possibilities?

ATW answers with a collection of visual layers created using a
flexible, hexagonal grid system inspired by the geometries of
Platonic solids and the tessellated works of M.C. Escher,
evoking themes of connection and illumination.

When combined, millions of prismatic possibilities await the
collector.

Take that, single song with single art.

And you—our audience—who are you? Will you be inspired to
become one of our 1000 true fans and join us on this journey?
Will you be moved to answer these questions yourself as an
artist?

We hope so.

Thank you for shining a light in the dark with us. Let’s see
where this path leads us.

QmQc9QPKdCi4uT1FYdvL6oCiwsn6wav5cgNrppxu.description:
15 years ago I wrote a song called “Say It’s Possible,” and the song changed my life. 

I went from an unknown artist to the most subscribed musician on YouTube at the time. Thousands of people around the world created their own cover videos of my song. I won the inaugural YouTube Award for Best Music Video, signed deals with Universal Music Publishing and Island Records, played solo at Wembley Stadium, toured all over Europe and the UK. My experience in the major label music industry was a whirlwind ride that ultimately did not serve my best interests, and it took years of dismantling, reprogramming, and letting go of painful experiences and toxic relationships in order to find my way back to my pure love of music and the joy that comes from sharing it. 

This year I reclaimed the rights to my earliest songs from Universal Music, with the intention of recording new versions and giving these songs a life they never had. I am starting with my Async Music project: an interactive, collaborative version of my song "Say It's Possible." There are 460 possible configurations of the song and corresponding visual art, ranging from pure acoustic guitar and vocals to a lush arrangement with 13 different layers of sound.

I wrote, played, and recorded all of the music in my home studio, creating the parts in a modular way, like a puzzle, knowing the track would have to make sense in any configuration. My dear friend MG O’Shea helped with the mix, carving out frequencies to ensure all the parts would sound excellent together, in any combination. Every mix begins in the same way, like the song itself began, with acoustic guitar and vocals, evolving into something more after the first verse. Some of the changes can be subtle and some can be striking. 

The visual art is a series of self-portraits I created in the process of freeing myself from the expectations and demands placed on me by an industry that did not support me as the innovative and individualistic artist that I am.

One collector can own the Master. Up to five collectors of the individual stems (vocals, guitar, drums + percussion, bass + strings, bells + synths) will control the master mix and album cover art. A limited number of “blank records”(2,000 silver, 10 gold, 3 platinum) are also available. You can collect a blank record in advance and mint your version as soon as you hear something you love. And if you do hear something you love, mint it at that time, because we might never stumble upon that particular mix again! 

These song versions and cover art will not be released anywhere outside of this project, and the NFT you collect will be a rare and unique piece of my history and evolution as a self-actualized, independent artist.
