QmR3yCwY2J5SWe2G6Ye3LcsCgXKrCg7456TafcYB.description:
A collection of unique, iconic, Proper Punks - the people featured in this collection were around in the early days of punk in the 1970's. Each image is a tribute to them. And also to Punk Rock, Crypto Art, Trash art, Glitch Art, Rebel Rock, Punk Art, Pop Art, Naïve Art, The Situationists, The Dadaists  and all the other underground, grass roots, music & art movements that have attempted to rock the system, affect change & champion creativity - here's to the mould-breakers. The square pegs, trying to fit into round holes. 

All art hand drawn by Angie Taylor - references taken from photographs owned by Angie Taylor or 3D models created by Angie Taylor. With the exception of the following images;
Image of Debbie Harry - Private Stock Records, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
Creative Commons Image of Jordan Mooney - Unknown author, CC BY-SA 4.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
Creative Commons image of Patti Smith - UCLA Library Special Collections, CC BY 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons

QmR5o8VCLkGK8geL691GsD2wzBjv59hNe1QxErNP.name: Protector Of The Chain
QmR5o8VCLkGK8geL691GsD2wzBjv59hNe1QxErNP.description:
”The separated lands were bound together by the chains of the gods. The communities living in the lands consisted of developed peoples that were different from each other. In the deepest area, called the bottom, there were sacred connections. Peaceful communities have not broken these two rules for centuries. The first rule is to protect your community, the second rule is to stay away from the Dip. Until the deep beings come to light. Communities had to come together and fight against incoming creatures to maintain their sacred bonds.”

Spirits Of The Mask

Isle of Mary is one of the four islands where there is water. It raises generations that have grown up with the old tales of female warriors. The last representatives of the human race live here. It is a hunter community that makes a living by producing silk and caftans. A mask is produced for every woman who, enters puberty. These masks are warrior spirits bestowed upon them by the gods. Masks protect them during war and suppress their conscientious maternal personalities, teaching them to be protective and just. Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. QmR78yxg2rmzZrN6s4K5CgUN4m7inGcuRYi62X25.name: GrandRising #36
QmR78yxg2rmzZrN6s4K5CgUN4m7inGcuRYi62X25.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmR7fB5VWppcbpnepQWDXppNRMZCw2Mw5xJPzZ9G.description:
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s masterpiece *Eine kleine Nachtmusik* ("a little night music") was completed in Vienna on 10 August 1787 while he worked on the opera Don Giovanni, but the work was not published until about 1827, long after his death. The occasion and the patron for Mozart’s composition remains unknown today and it was probably never performed within the span of his lifetime.

Almost 200 years later and in the same city of Vienna, the world’s musical capital, Mozart’s masterpiece has been remoulded to reflect society’s evolution into today’s postmodern artistic landscape, with the incorporation of bold and futuristic cutting-edge technologies.

The structure of the Mastertrack consists of four stems: Violin 1, Violin 2, Viola and Cello, with a total of five variations per stem. Layering different stem variations over one another leads to the creation of personally crafted, magical and unique tapestries of sound, closely related to Mozart’s original.

QmR9rjdgaDcBJ68zZMiMJ4KqckR4AYV5TJkaeHCe.name: பண் (Pann) Silver Edition (Mix: 124222100)
QmR9rjdgaDcBJ68zZMiMJ4KqckR4AYV5TJkaeHCe.description:
The seed of all melodies, "பண்" is the truest representation of Tamil music, culture, land and its people. A voyage that connects the past, beholds the present and accompanies into the future, Pann is the beginning of a journey into the world of performed, programmable art. This 30-minute piece of music written in Tamil, was commissioned and produced by Metapurse and is a first of its kind NFT from India. It had its premiere in New York’s Terminal 5 on the 4th of November 2021 at Dreamverse, the world’s largest NFT exhibition curated by Metapurse. Pann became the ambient music for this historic event that merged the physical and digital realms for the first time, showcasing the pinnacle of NFT art of more than 150 artists from around the world.

Woven from nine layers of music, each having several variants within it, the Pann master track captures a fresh collaborative performance of 40 musicians and visual artists.  It can be heard in 19440 different combinations, making it a dynamic piece of music with artwork done by Susha, Ghana N B and Vidhya Vijay that evolve along with every changing state of music. While most of the variants were recorded at 2barQ Studios, Chennai, Tamil Nadu by Sujith Sreedhar and Divine Joseph, the cherry on the cake is the live performance of some of the musical and art variants captured during the Dreamverse experience.

QmRAYWVMwT89sfWHkohSLkkQVQ2JaSf6U4Bjz9RU.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmRAhQDZjEaPHMWsjwqsccy7Z2xRmgN99fn7cz7C.name: GrandRising #156
QmRAhQDZjEaPHMWsjwqsccy7Z2xRmgN99fn7cz7C.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

618 tokens edition out of 3513840 possible generative iterations
2 styles, 14 layers with varying degrees of rarity
3 animated MP4 legendary editions

QmRBdNVTPBTM3JzC2oq9L63DCZazYD2PyZFd2qzW.name: GrandRising #0
QmRBdNVTPBTM3JzC2oq9L63DCZazYD2PyZFd2qzW.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmRCZaJT9Eh82fbcz9tgtQXJ6Tm2NBzgDtjBgzU8.name: Danktone S1E3 #202
QmRCZaJT9Eh82fbcz9tgtQXJ6Tm2NBzgDtjBgzU8.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmRCczHF95Fkk1iJUbhyJJ91eeGx7eQjKDKLzpbt.name: DANKTONE S1E5 #1
QmRCczHF95Fkk1iJUbhyJJ91eeGx7eQjKDKLzpbt.description:
In this episode of The Dankness, we dive into the world of C3, an artist who continues to push boundaries and risks it all to give a voice to the voiceless. Despite the strict anti-regime and crypto bans in Iran, C3's work has found its way into the hands of loyal collectors worldwide.  The Iranian-born enigmatic artist defies danger to share his powerful message through art and NFTs. We explore his journey from a regular job to becoming a successful full-time NFT artist, and the darkness and hardships he faced along the way.

Join us as we discuss C3's discovery of NFTs, his commitment to sharing the true stories behind his art, and the high stakes he faces in Iran for producing his work. Learn about the importance of building a cohesive body of work and how C3's kindness and empathy have shaped his experiences in the NFT space. Listen in as he shares valuable advice for new artists entering the world of NFTs and how forming genuine connections with like-minded individuals can make all the difference. You can learn more about C3 and his work at his website (c3naa.art) and be sure to follow him on Twitter @c3naaX.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft. 

But wait, theres more! Every episode comes with a free collectible audio/visual NFT created through a collaboration of our bandleader and audio wizard Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood) on Async art. We call them “Danktones” and they will be available as an open edition for a limited time after each episode. Head on over to thedankness.xyz to find out more.

QmRCe6bsVaG72PG4dgEbNy7dPx68t47KJFFe5SZ1.name: SATS #117
QmRCe6bsVaG72PG4dgEbNy7dPx68t47KJFFe5SZ1.description:
'Looking for Satoshi' is a project that sprouts from the layers and states I've painted on one wooden panel. From 2016 until 2020 I painted several portraits and minted a few of them on SuperRare. 

This project blends a bit of our meme culture and taps into the ancient craft of painting at the same time. It refers to our current financial state and brings an ode to artists I admire. 

When this blueprint is sold out, I will determine a date on which I will give away 'My two Satoshi's' : 
https://superrare.com/artwork-v2/'my-2-satoshis'-18110 + this particular panel to one lucky collector. 

I will use 'Wheel of Names' to pick a winner. 

To qualify for this draft, a collector needs to :

1: follow me on Twitter
2: add the address that holds the blueprint to a dedicated tweet that will be send into the world when the time is right. 


This blueprint also contains 3 legendaries which are part of the 'Bitcoin White Paper' series. This series will have 13 pieces that will be minted during 2023, more info can be found on the website.

Thank you for following me on this journey. 

May the SATS be with you!

QmRChcrHw1GDMmq8KWA38Mp6ycDVp9AToXSPFKTV.name: Mind Puzzle
QmRChcrHw1GDMmq8KWA38Mp6ycDVp9AToXSPFKTV.description:
Life is a big puzzle game made up of many different events and experiences, some of which are interrelated and overlap. The more experiences we gather, the more complex and colourful the overall picture becomes. 

But over time, the perception, emotional colouring and evaluation of different events and memories changes. Some things we may remember only vaguely after a while.

Thus, the inner thought puzzle of each individual constantly reflects life and yet is greater than the sum of its parts.

The work has been created as part of a conversation with my younger self and the search for my signature style, that I started in July 2020.

It is based on a ballpen drawing from about 1990, that I digitally recreated by accurately following the lines using a graphics drawing tablet. Next I filled the shapes with digital colors before I finally decided to split the work into several puzzle-pieces, that can be independently change hue or alternatively display the outlines to turn it into an interactive AsyncArt work.

QmRDXu1eECqiMudKpXrrRyC4wZe5MTpa6MMxyp8F.name: The Tree
QmRDXu1eECqiMudKpXrrRyC4wZe5MTpa6MMxyp8F.description: The trees are the structures connecting the biomorph figures and appear to be loosely related to the Tree of Life from Kabbalistic renown.  The manuscript records five tree variants that it deems "wise and proper" for universal disclosure.  Others are rumoured to exist.  - The Tree of the Seer -  The Lātō, the seer, is not themselves a genuine agent of power.  They are but a conduit.  The central triangle and its appendages represent their arms outstretched, ready to receive; and the disconnected northern triad is the all-seeing eye that is not the Lātō's own.  The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal an exhortation.  - The Tree of Chaos -  Kháos is a spider sinister and wise, though oft-broken in battle, always swift again to rise.  The Southern Monad represents the body of the creature, and the chaotic connections are its legs, neither as numerous as they once were, nor capable of finding the firm ground anymore.  Kháos when undisturbed walks its own internal landscapes, twisted and fraught with infinities that would drive lesser minds insane.  The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the arachnid's method of immortality.  - The Tree of Power -  Mek'ena is an ancient device of great power, ever wrong for its time.  The triaxial connection between the Northern Triad and the Southern Monad is the nexus of the machine's power.  The lateral connections to the Eastern and Western Triads are its stabilizers, without which it could very well destroy the world.  The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the source of all power.  - The Tree of Balance -  Tentsel is the scale of justice by which one and all are weighed.  Its dexterous half measures our acts of benevolence against our transgressions that burden the scale's sinister side.  The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the way to evade final judgment.  - The Tree of the Grail -  Aska is the grail filled by the fountain of wisdom.  Its connected parts are the wall of the grail, and the solitary remnant of the Northern Triad represents the water of life.  The markings on the connective lines, in addition to revealing hidden connections to learned scholars of the mystical, are rumoured to reveal the name of a people whose wisdom is lost unto time.

On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. QmRDwq7BKMyBEPMSJTQfnhwnm8V7caM9BEy2UXtV.name: LEAVING  Silver Edition (Mix: 312003)
QmRDwq7BKMyBEPMSJTQfnhwnm8V7caM9BEy2UXtV.description:
‘Leaving' is a dynamic musical artwork that represents a new frontier in what art and music is, and should do; an experiment in storytelling, in sonic possibilities, in the value of art, and in the relationship between audience, collector, artist and authorship. The stem owners control everything: who sings the vocal part and with what melodies; what drums underpin the performance; the melodies, and even the lyrics. All the variations made possible work together seamlessly such that the artwork includes 6400 unique compositions - not trivially different, but each one its very own song, with the potential to be anything from a piano ballad to a 1980s synth track, to a sample-heavy piece of modern electronica. Each stem-owner has the power to alter the whole master, without knowing what the other stem owners will do - collectors might collaboratively arrive at a genre by responding to each others’ choices, create a genre-spanning hybrid, or actively seek out the most disharmonious composition possible.

The song explores the different states of a unique relationship between three people; a love triangle told from the perspective of all those involved. The three characters interweave and blur into each other, with the different primary emotional states as represented by the instrumental, and the different sides of the story as told by the lyrics, intermingling with unpredictable results - eventually, past present, and future; the betrayed, the betrayer and the object of the betrayal; loss, guilt and hope; all meld into one. In this way, the master track will dynamically reflect the intricate complexity of love and loss. Each individual part has been separately written, performed and recorded in a decentralised fashion by HMLTD and our collaborators, Tallulah Eden and Seth Evans. Each unique composition is a snapshot of a different angle of the love triangle in both time and perspective. The accompanying cover art, beautifully rendered by our collaborator Mike Raymond, is the visual representation of ‘Leaving'. Each possible composition; each distinct moment in the relationship, has a corresponding and distinct visual representation: three lovers, 6400 different dances, spinning and looping around in eternity.

QmRER8QYKJbqkGCAq6pwzfgvGX7aGvzbyEZnTtYH.name: GrandRising #362
QmRER8QYKJbqkGCAq6pwzfgvGX7aGvzbyEZnTtYH.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmREWu2Z77qwVfJAq53HP9ZYYrv8yeYUvVGLPSHM.name: Say It's Possible Silver Edition (Mix: 20232)
QmREWu2Z77qwVfJAq53HP9ZYYrv8yeYUvVGLPSHM.description:
15 years ago I wrote a song called “Say It’s Possible,” and the song changed my life. 

I went from an unknown artist to the most subscribed musician on YouTube at the time. Thousands of people around the world created their own cover videos of my song. I won the inaugural YouTube Award for Best Music Video, signed deals with Universal Music Publishing and Island Records, played solo at Wembley Stadium, toured all over Europe and the UK. My experience in the major label music industry was a whirlwind ride that ultimately did not serve my best interests, and it took years of dismantling, reprogramming, and letting go of painful experiences and toxic relationships in order to find my way back to my pure love of music and the joy that comes from sharing it. 

This year I reclaimed the rights to my earliest songs from Universal Music, with the intention of recording new versions and giving these songs a life they never had. I am starting with my Async Music project: an interactive, collaborative version of my song "Say It's Possible." There are 460 possible configurations of the song and corresponding visual art, ranging from pure acoustic guitar and vocals to a lush arrangement with 13 different layers of sound.

I wrote, played, and recorded all of the music in my home studio, creating the parts in a modular way, like a puzzle, knowing the track would have to make sense in any configuration. My dear friend MG O’Shea helped with the mix, carving out frequencies to ensure all the parts would sound excellent together, in any combination. Every mix begins in the same way, like the song itself began, with acoustic guitar and vocals, evolving into something more after the first verse. Some of the changes can be subtle and some can be striking. 

The visual art is a series of self-portraits I created in the process of freeing myself from the expectations and demands placed on me by an industry that did not support me as the innovative and individualistic artist that I am.

One collector can own the Master. Up to five collectors of the individual stems (vocals, guitar, drums + percussion, bass + strings, bells + synths) will control the master mix and album cover art. A limited number of “blank records”(2,000 silver, 10 gold, 3 platinum) are also available. You can collect a blank record in advance and mint your version as soon as you hear something you love. And if you do hear something you love, mint it at that time, because we might never stumble upon that particular mix again! 

These song versions and cover art will not be released anywhere outside of this project, and the NFT you collect will be a rare and unique piece of my history and evolution as a self-actualized, independent artist.

QmREZ2BvbJepvK4kM7fb1gPCRwsZbGp4PMYozhpR.name: Inaccessible World #408
QmREZ2BvbJepvK4kM7fb1gPCRwsZbGp4PMYozhpR.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmRFQN288gik5c7Lr7JRktPAkNE2pfFPDcBkkzL1.description:
The final iteration of an ongoing series of symbols, figures and mandalas since 2015. The EX_VISIONES blueprint can manifest three different types.

TRANSMUTATIONAL ARCHETYPE:
a timeless unification of the organic and synthetic. A perception of all things both abstract, and definite. A vague reproduction, which is both perfect, and imperfect. A memory of a piece of reality and something inconceivable. 

META_ANIMA:
the anticipated embodiment of the self beyond physical limitations. Every colour, element, and space revolves around the psyche, perpetually mutable.

ILLUMINATUS CONSCIENTIA:
a singular visual vibration of enlightenment.
Each mandala is a stage toward a conscious state.

QmRFZBpbR8hvZLAw3GbDyYY2gU6yUptyKicAH1xt.name: Digital Device June 2020
QmRFZBpbR8hvZLAw3GbDyYY2gU6yUptyKicAH1xt.description:
Sometimes, things happen by chance or coincidence. During the lockdown of the Covid-19 pandemic, I’ve experimented with textures, colors, and optical effects - and an AI software. The aim of this optical study was to see what sensations it could provoke and explore the state of “controlled confusion” it could create, while keeping it simple.
One of the first results of my optical experimentation is this Digital Device. Starting from single lines of various thicknesses, I played with repetition and chromatic clashes, soon realizing these very simple elements could open infinite possibilities and generate countless patterns: the experiment could not be interrupted.
While thinking back at Bruno Munari and the Italian season of Arte Programmata (programmed art) of the 1960s, I looked at the programmable future of it, finding in Async the perfect solution for keeping my artistic exploration and this historical movement alive. Only this time it is the collectors who can play the creator’s part, having the chance to write a new page in the history of programmable art.
To learn more about the creative process and the relevance of this Digital Device in relation to the tradition of Arte Programmata you can check out the brief manual at http://www.mattiac.it/mattiac_dd1_async.pdf

QmRFqtHrw4iKxU7AwddhZoM9mURsox1tczsntqGr.name: Deathless #4
QmRFqtHrw4iKxU7AwddhZoM9mURsox1tczsntqGr.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmRFuef6YKMkv5jeZZbZs2YQTz4akwvaQNSnrJer.name: பண் (Pann) Silver Edition (Mix: 000000000)
QmRFuef6YKMkv5jeZZbZs2YQTz4akwvaQNSnrJer.description:
The seed of all melodies, "பண்" is the truest representation of Tamil music, culture, land and its people. A voyage that connects the past, beholds the present and accompanies into the future, Pann is the beginning of a journey into the world of performed, programmable art. This 30-minute piece of music written in Tamil, was commissioned and produced by Metapurse and is a first of its kind NFT from India. It had its premiere in New York’s Terminal 5 on the 4th of November 2021 at Dreamverse, the world’s largest NFT exhibition curated by Metapurse. Pann became the ambient music for this historic event that merged the physical and digital realms for the first time, showcasing the pinnacle of NFT art of more than 150 artists from around the world.

Woven from nine layers of music, each having several variants within it, the Pann master track captures a fresh collaborative performance of 40 musicians and visual artists.  It can be heard in 19440 different combinations, making it a dynamic piece of music with artwork done by Susha, Ghana N B and Vidhya Vijay that evolve along with every changing state of music. While most of the variants were recorded at 2barQ Studios, Chennai, Tamil Nadu by Sujith Sreedhar and Divine Joseph, the cherry on the cake is the live performance of some of the musical and art variants captured during the Dreamverse experience.

QmRG7VrPPUi32wf6J3cvUCzYnXMu2XL3FvXs1ecE.description:

This project blends a bit of our meme culture and taps into the ancient craft of painting at the same time. It refers to our current financial state and brings an ode to artists I admire. 

When this blueprint is sold out, I will determine a date on which I will give away 'My two Satoshi's' : 
https://superrare.com/artwork-v2/'my-2-satoshis'-18110 + this particular panel to one lucky collector. 

I will use 'Wheel of Names' to pick a winner. 

To qualify for this draft, a collector needs to :

1: follow me on Twitter
2: add the address that holds the blueprint to a dedicated tweet that will be send into the world when the time is right. 


This blueprint also contains 3 legendaries which are part of the 'Bitcoin White Paper' series. This series will have 13 pieces that will be minted during 2023, more info can be found on the website.

Thank you for following me on this journey. 

May the SATS be with you!

QmRGLioPUzzsRNFczzX8ZqpioEjBQCpdt8pJ89TG.name: GrandRising #7
QmRGLioPUzzsRNFczzX8ZqpioEjBQCpdt8pJ89TG.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmRJ1zyjvM2yTurGK7nNXf6hdD2n6V4UHSMgJrBb.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

Danktone 003 created through a collaboration of audio wizard Asa Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood).

QmRJA8fsrk1DhxwAmNKsacKcLaa8GMDkiKxxqGwv.name: பண் (Pann) Silver Edition (Mix: 014112100)
QmRJA8fsrk1DhxwAmNKsacKcLaa8GMDkiKxxqGwv.description:
The seed of all melodies, "பண்" is the truest representation of Tamil music, culture, land and its people. A voyage that connects the past, beholds the present and accompanies into the future, Pann is the beginning of a journey into the world of performed, programmable art. This 30-minute piece of music written in Tamil, was commissioned and produced by Metapurse and is a first of its kind NFT from India. It had its premiere in New York’s Terminal 5 on the 4th of November 2021 at Dreamverse, the world’s largest NFT exhibition curated by Metapurse. Pann became the ambient music for this historic event that merged the physical and digital realms for the first time, showcasing the pinnacle of NFT art of more than 150 artists from around the world.

Woven from nine layers of music, each having several variants within it, the Pann master track captures a fresh collaborative performance of 40 musicians and visual artists.  It can be heard in 19440 different combinations, making it a dynamic piece of music with artwork done by Susha, Ghana N B and Vidhya Vijay that evolve along with every changing state of music. While most of the variants were recorded at 2barQ Studios, Chennai, Tamil Nadu by Sujith Sreedhar and Divine Joseph, the cherry on the cake is the live performance of some of the musical and art variants captured during the Dreamverse experience.

Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. QmRK4hZes4cvfmE2GDrfpBVELMNnhJCVr72TA9Vf.description:
Welcome back to The Dankness, your go-to destination for all things crypto art and culture. This week, we've got a special guest that's going to blow your mind. Carlos Marcial is an amazing 3D artist, known for his infinitely looping masterpieces that tackle themes of governmental power and corruption. His work celebrates decentralized currency and crypto culture and it often contains reference to 20th-century art and artists.

In this episode, Carlos opens up about balancing his art career with the responsibilities of being a husband and a dad, and how crypto art has opened up doors for him that were previously closed in the traditional art world. He's also teaching himself to code and has a new generative art project in the works that's sure to make waves 🐚

Carlos is not one to shy away from speaking his mind, and his straightforward and unapologetic approach to art and life is what makes him one of our favorite people in the digital art space. You need to follow Carlos at @carlosmarcialt on Twitter and you can find some of his best work on SuperRare at superrare.com/carlosmarcial.

Before we dive in with Carlos, Dan and Jason talk Meme Wars, what it’s like to make a documentary about crypto art, and the influx of prompt-driven AI art. So buckle up, because this episode is going to be a wild ride! 

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft. 

But wait, theres more! Every episode comes with a free collectible audio/visual NFT created through a collaboration of our bandleader and audio wizard Stella (@stellaphonic) and visionary digital artist FFFFlood (@fffflood) on Async art. We call them “Danktones” and they will be available as an open edition for a limited time after each episode. Head on over to thedankness.xyz to find out more.

QmRL5NBjeBRKhFFhE4ibdHGFaajL1mb1KoK7ik8j.name: Drums
QmRL5NBjeBRKhFFhE4ibdHGFaajL1mb1KoK7ik8j.description:
Drum layer of PLS&TY’s “Ride or Die”

“Ride or Die” is PLS&TY’s newest single release in collaboration with Barbados-born soul singer, Bobby Saint. 

Tommy Leas, a Florida native - better known as PLS&TY - is burgeoning into the electronic dance music scene with his unique sound: languid bass, captivating vocals and enough upbeat melodies to make anybody feel good. After a collection of chart topping singles including "Good Vibes" (#1 on iTunes US Electronic Charts), "Down For Me", "Rebel Love (#1 on iTunes US Electronic Charts), and "Motives" (#1 on iTunes US Electronic Charts / Top 25 Billboard Electronic Charts), PLS&TY would see his productions Remixed by Grammy nominated Morgan Page, Rusko, Cazzette, Bondax, YehMe2 (Josh from Flosstradamus latest venture), and more. 

His music has amassed over 100 million listens across streaming platforms, and has been placed in nationally airing television commercials, including a Hershey's Chocolate campaign which has been viewed over 1 BILLION times. Prior to “Ride or Die”, PLS&TY kept busy with a 2019 touring season that included A-List electronic festivals Shaky Beats, Breakaway, Electric Forest, EDC Vegas, & more, along with the release of his “Very Special” EP, which included pop records with artists like Sean Kingston, Wifisfuneral, & Alex Aiono (of Netflix’s “Finding Ohana”).

“Ride or Die” is a summertime, feel-good single that encompasses love & romance. Saint’s vocals lead listeners to imagine time spent in tropical paradise with their partner. Now in programmable format on Async Music, users can select alternate variations of the stems that comprise the master track. In this way, the master track dynamically shifts and promotes adventure, like the upbeat tune itself that is “Ride or Die”.

QmRLFkaF3DnSxW9vnLTb4DUDQFT7EcBk47qY1yDb.description:
A sudden vision rushes through the mind: it might turn into a pleasant experience, grow into an annoying, recurring thought, shatter your mind into pieces, and stay there persistently. 

I want to record some of these visionary bits and record them. Analog videotapes have been used extensively to record paranormal activities. The way this technology is built gives a wide range of possibilities to document sightings of unearthly entities. 

SPECTRAL VISIONS is built from images created on analog video processing gear which allows exploring textures generated in the process of bending the video signal. I am using my own drawings and portraits as a bridge to meet the matter of spectral entities within me.

QmRLSbpuhdftcyH7kJznhE2V98Mb1FuY91vjrt49.name: 3x3 #14
QmRLSbpuhdftcyH7kJznhE2V98Mb1FuY91vjrt49.description:
Named for the blend mode that inspired its creation, 'Multiply' makes liberal use of this digital composition method in its construction.

This piece consists of several hand-painted layers that overlap and mask each other in various ways. Each new 3x3 grid of colour reacts with those that came before it, before being wrapped in additional tone, border, and texture. The finished, fully-blended artwork has almost 50 billion unique possible combinations.

All artwork is 3840x3840 pixel resolution, and 5250 × 5250 'originals' are available to edition owners on request.

QmRLUiHPdDRYGzRWzzzjAP8ZiWUzJjRJD6hcPgmP.name: Digital Collectible #47
QmRLUiHPdDRYGzRWzzzjAP8ZiWUzJjRJD6hcPgmP.description:
A groundbreaking collaboration between Alma Deutscher, the 17 years-old prodigy composer, conductor, pianist and violinist, and Ekaterina Lestienne, a French digital artist famous for her colorful creations full of positive vibes.  

Alma’s digital collectibles is based on Alma’s yet unreleased ‘The Emperor’s New Waltz’, a musical romantic-comedy about the timeless story of a rich girl falling for a poor boy, the class struggle and how love conquers all. World premiere of Alma Deutscher's upcoming opera to be premiered in Salzburg in 2023!  

The collection features 400 individual unique pieces that are generated from unique combinations of four music themes: Jonas’ Waltz, Love duet, Leonie’s song and Kaiser’s song, with accompanying vibrant visual themes that tell the same story. There are 4 legendary editions within the entire collection with some exceptional utilities.

https://www.almasdigitalcollectibles.com 

Music: Alma Deutscher 
Visuals: Ekaterina Lestienne 
Orchestra: Strauss Capelle Vienna 
Producer: Josip Susnjara / Vienna Digital Lab
Recording Studio: Treehouse Studios Vienna 

Vienna Digital Lab, 2022
https://www.vdl.art

Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. QmRLjoFuqu7PuNngRgrr6YH3gr9wddDCe5eHuRZu.name: Seaship #10
QmRLjoFuqu7PuNngRgrr6YH3gr9wddDCe5eHuRZu.description:
2023 Leagues Under the Sea in the second in a series of digital colleges exploring and developing my vision of what The Metaverse (as a place to inhabit) means to me. I am a worldbuilder and storyteller, and these works enable me to envision the possibilities for its appearance, which heretofore has existed only in my imagination. Through the process of creation, a three dimensional world takes shape,emerging out of a wholly individual personal perspective which then becomes visible to others, when presented in digital form.

In the first project, I discovered that for me, The Metaverse exists in the ether, formless and invisible in the space Between Dimensions. In this project, I embark an undersea voyage seeking to expand and build upon that vision.

On my journey, I discovered that the leagues under the sea are one of the least explored expanses on Earth. There are no acres to build upon, no air to breathe. There is only soundlessness and frigid darkness in depths that are lacking in highways and byways, where predators glide freely in multiple directions, appearing silently out of the cold blackness in front of your face like weightless ghosts. 

There is an enormous sensation of a lack of control over one's environment and one's circumstances. How similar this feeling is to the one I've been having in response to the destruction and havoc wrought upon the space in the past several months. How similar the feeling of drowning. 

And yet, in the feeling of drowning, there is treasure to be found. Venturing into the depths changes you. And, unlike the world beneath the seas, and most importantly, The Metaverse is built on the foundation of an ethos that cannot be buried by either the incoming tides nor the shifting sands. 

Featuring a bunch of punks (and a seasick pepe) by cryptoartists Eric Rhodes @ericprhodes, Brandon Walsh @NFTWannabe, acid star @acidstarart and janestik.wtf @janestik

QmRMg2d3kgYFM2nyku2dJg28KXojCRzMLFnzjyYk.name: Deathless #19
QmRMg2d3kgYFM2nyku2dJg28KXojCRzMLFnzjyYk.description:
In the beginning, there was nothing.

 The world was empty and void, black and grey,  shade and dusk. Nothing moved, nothing shifted, all was owned by The Dark. But nature is more powerful, more unknowable, more unpredictable, than any of us can imagine, and so one day, defying all odds, among The Dark, a child was born. One that was different. One that, they knew, was dangerous. 

Her true name is lost to history and the pages it was first written on. But us, we know her as Light, the first of the spectrum, the mother of all colours. As she grew, in strength and wisdom, The Dark grew more afraid, more weary of this new child in their ranks. It was why till this day the shadows fear the sun. 

Soon, a plan was hatched, to destroy their daughter, their abominable creation. A dagger of Obsidian was made, moulded from the darkest metals, the blackest materials, all to down their biggest threat. Sensing danger, Light did the only thing she could: she went to the mountains of Prisma, at the edge of all they knew, and jumped, scattering herself, her essence into 7 different parts. Her children. 

They were old and young, large and small, all with their different temperaments. These were the first of those who would wage war on their mother’s behalf. 

And we, called them The Deathless. 

The ones who didn’t die. 

The ones who had never lived. 
.
The Deathless is my hit 1/1 series, exploring the depth of color and their origins. In my Async genesis, I take that concept and turn it over on its head, creating, for the first time, an expansive canvas for everyone to explore the story I began three years ago.

QmRMnNDKe56LcXVmAYfAm4fH9HaYaXGj8TdNeW9H.name: Landscape Study #1 (with Visitor)
QmRMnNDKe56LcXVmAYfAm4fH9HaYaXGj8TdNeW9H.description:
In the spirit of British landscape artists - your Constables, Turners, and Wilsons - this programmable painting features studies of breathtaking parts of the UK.

Views such as these are rarely empty of modern human activity. More popular areas are likely to receive an overwhelming number of visitors, though some might see just a few each day.

From ornately-framed originals in national gallery spaces, to an unframed canvas reproduction hung in your grandparent's kitchen - romantic landscape paintings can be found in a broad range of settings, and are often regarded as timeless.

A key inspiration for this particular artwork is Anglesey Abbey - a National Trust property in Cambridge, UK - which has an entire wing seemingly dedicated to Lord Fairhaven's collection of Windsor Castle paintings.

QmRNR14t8Kcs65TEiDCpJc5i8DdaUC8M6gDFVTxQ.name: பண் (Pann) Silver Edition (Mix: 033211011)
QmRNR14t8Kcs65TEiDCpJc5i8DdaUC8M6gDFVTxQ.description:
The seed of all melodies, "பண்" is the truest representation of Tamil music, culture, land and its people. A voyage that connects the past, beholds the present and accompanies into the future, Pann is the beginning of a journey into the world of performed, programmable art. This 30-minute piece of music written in Tamil, was commissioned and produced by Metapurse and is a first of its kind NFT from India. It had its premiere in New York’s Terminal 5 on the 4th of November 2021 at Dreamverse, the world’s largest NFT exhibition curated by Metapurse. Pann became the ambient music for this historic event that merged the physical and digital realms for the first time, showcasing the pinnacle of NFT art of more than 150 artists from around the world.

Woven from nine layers of music, each having several variants within it, the Pann master track captures a fresh collaborative performance of 40 musicians and visual artists.  It can be heard in 19440 different combinations, making it a dynamic piece of music with artwork done by Susha, Ghana N B and Vidhya Vijay that evolve along with every changing state of music. While most of the variants were recorded at 2barQ Studios, Chennai, Tamil Nadu by Sujith Sreedhar and Divine Joseph, the cherry on the cake is the live performance of some of the musical and art variants captured during the Dreamverse experience.

QmRNx6tFUh7vXGAYNS78nzgZYL8VYvPMZoTP2knp.name: GrandRising #99
QmRNx6tFUh7vXGAYNS78nzgZYL8VYvPMZoTP2knp.description:
Digging in the Blockchain (D.I.T.B.) has never felt so much like Diggin In The Crates (D.I.T.C.) This collection can be looked at as vinyl record warehouse named GRAND RISING, holding over 300,000 unique records, and the collectors can only leave with 420 copies. 

Then the warehouse is destroyed.

Using music inputs created by Rare Scrilla & RoomInEight, the collectors are participating in creating these compositions by hitting the Mint Button. Essentially making a collaboration with  Async's music generator. The artwork was created by Rare Scrilla and is based on vinyl record collecting, which Scrilla has been doing for over 20 years. 

You may find yourself with a coveted Obi Strip. Some familiar and non- familiar names may show up on the records as you peruse the collection. Scrilla, who's been a DJ, record producer, and artist his whole life, will sometimes put stickers on the vinyl, or doodles on the cover, sometimes the records get worn out, and sometimes while digging he may find a record with a graphic error or a different version of a song that was published and distributed by someone else. These details have been thoughtfully used while creating this collection. The easter eggs are plentiful.

Kane Mayfield and DJ Q-Bert both lend their skills on certain rarer tracks. You may find a legendary from Fake Sketch or K-Beta, maybe an epic guitar rendition featuring Glenn Yeah. The only way to pull these records from the crates is to hit that mint button.

Scrilla, also known for his Rare Pepes and Fake Rares, dating back to when he began "tokenizing" art and music using the Bitcoin blockchain in 2016, brings some of that to some of the art and music as well. But, of course, like the best Pepes should be- They are Rare outputs.

Some record are denominated in Sats, some in ETH, some in BTC, and of course yer local record dealer will sometimes deal in Pepecash.

There are plans to press up the best songs, curated by YOU - the collector, and put the album on Digital Streaming Platforms (DSPs.)  Let's see what transpires from it all.

QmRP1JUwpNHJq1VoMN6ADfs1AHGbnBqx8g2h5DiX.name: Inaccessible World #343
QmRP1JUwpNHJq1VoMN6ADfs1AHGbnBqx8g2h5DiX.description:
When a game fails, sometimes mid-crash you get a glimpse of a place that cannot persist. Sometimes if you manipulate some variables just right, you can teleport yourself into places that are walled-off from our experience by a barrier of cascading failure, corrupted worlds propped up by machinery that is whirring and overheating and dissipating fast as we try to take in the reality that is sliding back into the void.

These are glimpses of worlds that don't function, visions of places and times that could not persist as they were and are instead captured as still frames. This is satisfying the urge to take that glimpse of a beautiful failure and keep it - to crystallize into a transitory vision of a beautiful collapse.

More precisely - these are collections of pixels from manipulated NES games. Changing the hex code and crossing states with other games, repeating, stacking saves and layouts. Inaccessible Worlds is a broad project featuring different versions of the worlds, different formats of the art and conceptual work.

QmRPVDji9UeYTqWWcgVL28jsiWwo4bsoADkJTpf8.description:
Named for the blend mode that inspired its creation, 'Multiply' makes liberal use of this digital composition method in its construction.

This piece consists of several hand-painted layers that overlap and mask each other in various ways. Each new 3x3 grid of colour reacts with those that came before it, before being wrapped in additional tone, border, and texture. The finished, fully-blended artwork has almost 50 billion unique possible combinations.

All artwork is 3840x3840 pixel resolution, and 5250 × 5250 'originals' are available to edition owners on request.

Can you hear the voices of the past?

Inspired by the rich, eclectic, diverse, and often violent history of New Orleans, this collection harkens back to the French Quarter of the late 19th century. Resplendent with wrought iron, gas lamps, and masquerade balls, the past comes alive in this atmospheric composition celebrating the spirit of n0la.

J. Thorn has licensed n0la as CC0 or “No Rights Reserved,” waiving all rights to the work and placing the project as completely as possible in the public domain, so that others may freely build upon, enhance, and reuse the works for any purposes without restriction under copyright or database law.

Each audio & visual layers have been designed to interplay with one another resulting in thousands of unique possiblitlies.

Syntax [Two] is part of the new F.U.S.E. Syntax release that will be available on all music streaming platforms on June 4th.

The release will also include a special version, "Syntax [Two] @username Async NFT mix" which will be determined by from the current Master Track state one week after the sale of the Master and all layers. Welcome to Playerz Cardz. At its core, Playerz Cardz is a generative audio/visual NFT project powered by Async.Art. When you mint a Playerz Cardz pack, you will receive a unique piece of artwork combined with a full downloadable track. 

Each stem/visual layer combination is a fictional musician complete with a bio and backstory. The visual representation of these players shows up as collector cards. The artwork was generated using Midjourney and further processed with Photoshop and Lightroom. The music was composed, produced, and mixed by myself and pre-mastered by Genzo Rubin. Combined, these players make up a full band and a pack of cards. The categories are divided into Drums, Bass, Lead, Chords, Percussion, and EFX.

QmRQMkrfZif88SEmtyEBLzfgK6yu5sQKqBB64zv4.name: Burning
QmRQMkrfZif88SEmtyEBLzfgK6yu5sQKqBB64zv4.description:
Burning = The Urge To Create. There's always something brewing inside. Always an idea, an image or a plan to work on. Always a face to spend time with. To see the beauty and take the power to transform it into something else. I'm looking for unity in the World of a Scatterbrain. I flow through colors and find Peace inside my work. The progress, doing the work, the feeling when I step outside time. It's all captured in my work. Dense and Intense. Looking for details that light up and want to be discovered. Like diamonds in a mine.

The layers of this piece all have 2 states. The layer owners can choose which one will be visible. When Smoking, Holding, Staring and Flaying are together switched to State #2 they block the background image and become a New Piece. The layer owners have to work together if they want to see this piece. 


I want every layer owner to have the feeling they own something special that can also be shown just by itself. We all contribute to a larger system, but have our own thoughts and feelings too. I mean, we're all part of a family but we're also individuals. Like the transformers. 



Extra info:
I've burned the Base Drawing of this work in order to extracted value offline and added it to the online world. 

I set the drawing on fire in my garden and recorded the process. I've tokenized it and published it in an edition of 10 on Rarible and will give them away to a lucky few.

QmRR3cgQUxpGevCcNMygYpEkLXR2vnZZpLxQ3KnZ.name: Right Place & Right Time (Bitcoin Hourly Price Offset)
QmRR3cgQUxpGevCcNMygYpEkLXR2vnZZpLxQ3KnZ.description: Each day, a new composition for the Master is generated autonomously using a data feed of Bitcoin's last 24 hours of price action. Each hour's price programmatically controls rotation, scale, and position of a correlating layer. Astute viewers will surmise the day's price volatility simply by examining the artwork. While the daily image generation is the result of autonomous API calls, utilizing an algorithm the artist wrote, the artist has chosen to retain a control token. This token allows him to fine-tune variables associated with his algorithm, in addition to addressing aesthetic concerns within the life-cycle of the artwork. Layer state, alpha, hue, saturation, and brightness are elements the artist has retained control of in order that this artwork remain a living work-in-progress.\n\nAn earlier iteration of this artwork was featured as a nightly projection mapping video on the face of the Daniels Fisher Clocktower, as part of ETH Denver 2020. Access to this and additional exclusive content awaits the master token owner at the artist's NFT Portal: https://collect.mattkane.com/minted-works/right-place-right-time-bitcoin-hourly-price-offset/

QmRRJThbdWCvZyoomK6vN2FrefUT7cZCv4GfV854.description:
Named for the blend mode that inspired its creation, 'Multiply' makes liberal use of this digital composition method in its construction.

This piece consists of several hand-painted layers that overlap and mask each other in various ways. Each new 3x3 grid of colour reacts with those that came before it, before being wrapped in additional tone, border, and texture. The finished, fully-blended artwork has almost 50 billion unique possible combinations.

All artwork is 3840x3840 pixel resolution, and 5250 × 5250 'originals' are available to edition owners on request.

QmRSSJ1kYrtwc9G5mjHFhvqkdXpi5ERsLkf1vmqT.name: Say It's Possible Silver Edition (Mix: 00000)
QmRSSJ1kYrtwc9G5mjHFhvqkdXpi5ERsLkf1vmqT.description:
15 years ago I wrote a song called “Say It’s Possible,” and the song changed my life. 

I went from an unknown artist to the most subscribed musician on YouTube at the time. Thousands of people around the world created their own cover videos of my song. I won the inaugural YouTube Award for Best Music Video, signed deals with Universal Music Publishing and Island Records, played solo at Wembley Stadium, toured all over Europe and the UK. My experience in the major label music industry was a whirlwind ride that ultimately did not serve my best interests, and it took years of dismantling, reprogramming, and letting go of painful experiences and toxic relationships in order to find my way back to my pure love of music and the joy that comes from sharing it. 

This year I reclaimed the rights to my earliest songs from Universal Music, with the intention of recording new versions and giving these songs a life they never had. I am starting with my Async Music project: an interactive, collaborative version of my song "Say It's Possible." There are 460 possible configurations of the song and corresponding visual art, ranging from pure acoustic guitar and vocals to a lush arrangement with 13 different layers of sound.

I wrote, played, and recorded all of the music in my home studio, creating the parts in a modular way, like a puzzle, knowing the track would have to make sense in any configuration. My dear friend MG O’Shea helped with the mix, carving out frequencies to ensure all the parts would sound excellent together, in any combination. Every mix begins in the same way, like the song itself began, with acoustic guitar and vocals, evolving into something more after the first verse. Some of the changes can be subtle and some can be striking. 

The visual art is a series of self-portraits I created in the process of freeing myself from the expectations and demands placed on me by an industry that did not support me as the innovative and individualistic artist that I am.

One collector can own the Master. Up to five collectors of the individual stems (vocals, guitar, drums + percussion, bass + strings, bells + synths) will control the master mix and album cover art. A limited number of “blank records”(2,000 silver, 10 gold, 3 platinum) are also available. You can collect a blank record in advance and mint your version as soon as you hear something you love. And if you do hear something you love, mint it at that time, because we might never stumble upon that particular mix again! 

These song versions and cover art will not be released anywhere outside of this project, and the NFT you collect will be a rare and unique piece of my history and evolution as a self-actualized, independent artist.

QmRSTmeENayywgcDtWACpXMZxBWCfgRVq4QvWHBc.name: Danktone S1E3 #1117
QmRSTmeENayywgcDtWACpXMZxBWCfgRVq4QvWHBc.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.

To keep up with the podcast follow @thedanknessxyz on Twitter. Sickles is on Twitter at @dan_sickles and you can keep up with his amazing documentary at @newherexyz as it evolves. Artnome lives on Twitter at @artnome and his company ClubNFT, which helps collectors protect and discover NFTs, is at @club_nft.

QmRSaTi4s42Nra5kaFwJMoevhAJbwRwRVzvQXm1v.name: Say It's Possible Silver Edition (Mix: 11332)
QmRSaTi4s42Nra5kaFwJMoevhAJbwRwRVzvQXm1v.description:
15 years ago I wrote a song called “Say It’s Possible,” and the song changed my life. 

I went from an unknown artist to the most subscribed musician on YouTube at the time. Thousands of people around the world created their own cover videos of my song. I won the inaugural YouTube Award for Best Music Video, signed deals with Universal Music Publishing and Island Records, played solo at Wembley Stadium, toured all over Europe and the UK. My experience in the major label music industry was a whirlwind ride that ultimately did not serve my best interests, and it took years of dismantling, reprogramming, and letting go of painful experiences and toxic relationships in order to find my way back to my pure love of music and the joy that comes from sharing it. 

This year I reclaimed the rights to my earliest songs from Universal Music, with the intention of recording new versions and giving these songs a life they never had. I am starting with my Async Music project: an interactive, collaborative version of my song "Say It's Possible." There are 460 possible configurations of the song and corresponding visual art, ranging from pure acoustic guitar and vocals to a lush arrangement with 13 different layers of sound.

I wrote, played, and recorded all of the music in my home studio, creating the parts in a modular way, like a puzzle, knowing the track would have to make sense in any configuration. My dear friend MG O’Shea helped with the mix, carving out frequencies to ensure all the parts would sound excellent together, in any combination. Every mix begins in the same way, like the song itself began, with acoustic guitar and vocals, evolving into something more after the first verse. Some of the changes can be subtle and some can be striking. 

The visual art is a series of self-portraits I created in the process of freeing myself from the expectations and demands placed on me by an industry that did not support me as the innovative and individualistic artist that I am.

One collector can own the Master. Up to five collectors of the individual stems (vocals, guitar, drums + percussion, bass + strings, bells + synths) will control the master mix and album cover art. A limited number of “blank records”(2,000 silver, 10 gold, 3 platinum) are also available. You can collect a blank record in advance and mint your version as soon as you hear something you love. And if you do hear something you love, mint it at that time, because we might never stumble upon that particular mix again! 

These song versions and cover art will not be released anywhere outside of this project, and the NFT you collect will be a rare and unique piece of my history and evolution as a self-actualized, independent artist.

QmRT4HY8x5r2qf39QpT72p4JxamwQXWfQkfhYvnt.description:
On this episode we are honored to speak with artist and crypto art community activist Matt Kane! Matt is a self taught programmer who came to coding as a way to better actualize his artist visions through his own custom software. His work features dense multi-layered works that bring to mind complex, intricate, mesh-like, webs or networks. Matt is perhaps best known for his tremendously successful 2021 Art Blocks project “Gazers.” With Gazers, the works respond to the cycles of the moon and are perpetually shifting, making these works collectors want to live with and regularly revisit.   

In this episode, we discuss Matt’s journey from “lurker” to leader in the Cryptoart movement. Matt is candid about early successes and struggles to make it as an artist and the positive opportunities Cryptoart opened up for him. We learn where his interest in currency as a theme in his art stems from and his discovery of crypto. He also shares his love of art history and how analog painters like Monet serve as inspiration for his digital works. Matt shares an important story detailing how he collaborated with other important members of the crypto art community in 2020 to successfully lobby for a minimum secondary resale standard for artists. The Dankness is grateful to Matt for sharing so much of his story, it’s a special and insightful conversation, and we hope you find it as engaging as we did!   

You should absolutely follow Matt Kane at @MattKaneArtist and you can learn more about his unique and engaging body of work on his website mattkane.com.
